Type-I (the three triangle vertices [chi_i]) is the meeting point of the two minus-lines L_{sigma_j}, L_{sigma_k} (both contained in X) and lies on exactly one of the three plus-plane cubics, namely E_{sigma_i}. Type-II (the three points of R = X n l_V) lies on all three plus-plane cubics E_{sigma_1}, E_{sigma_2}, E_{sigma_3} and on none of the three minus-lines; it also lies on the V4-fixed line l_V, which is a positive-dimensional component of Fix(V4, P^4) but is NOT contained in X.
